Prorate costs by day

Source: R/prorate_costs_by_day.R
prorate_costs_by_day.Rd

Given a data frame of claims with cost data from claims which potentially span multiple days, this function will prorate the costs evenly over the duration of the claim.

Usage

prorate_costs_by_day(cost_data_frame)

Arguments

cost_data_frame

data frame of cost data created by a get_*_*_*costs function

Value

A data frame with costs prorated, with the original variable name changed.

Details

The original cost variables will be removed, and replaced by variables with the same name but with "_PRORATED" added to the variable name.

The amount columns processed are those returned by get_PS_CLM_costs(), get_IN_CLM_costs(), get_PS_REV_costs() and get_IN_REV_costs(): CLM_PMT_AMT, CARR_CLM_PRMRY_PYR_PD_AMT, NCH_CLM_PRVDR_PMT_AMT, NCH_CLM_BENE_PMT_AMT, NCH_CARR_SBMT_CHRG_AMT, NCH_CARR_ALOW_CHRG_AMT, CARR_CLM_CASH_DDCTBL_APPLY_AMT, CLM_TOT, CLM_AMT, SBMTCH, ALOWCH, PMTAMT, REV_CH and REVPMT, and the same columns with _ADJUSTED added by adjust_costs_for_inflation(). Other columns are kept unchanged on every day of the claim.

A claim whose CLM_FROM or CLM_THRU is missing, or whose CLM_THRU is before its CLM_FROM, cannot be spread over days. It is left out of the result, with a warning giving how many claims were left out for each reason, so prorated totals can fall short of the input.

Examples

claims <- data.frame(
  USRDS_ID = c(1, 2),
  CLM_FROM = as.Date(c("2010-01-01", "2010-02-01")),
  CLM_THRU = as.Date(c("2010-01-03", "2010-02-01")),
  PMTAMT = c(30, 20)
)
prorate_costs_by_day(claims)
#>   USRDS_ID   CLM_FROM   CLM_THRU service_date PMTAMT_PRORATED
#> 1        1 2010-01-01 2010-01-03   2010-01-01              10
#> 2        1 2010-01-01 2010-01-03   2010-01-02              10
#> 3        1 2010-01-01 2010-01-03   2010-01-03              10
#> 4        2 2010-02-01 2010-02-01   2010-02-01              20
